title: Governance pre-authorizes a yield band rather than a rate, letting operators move the savings rate without a new approval
content:
The Savings risk parameters pair two numbers that do different jobs: "Max yield: 5%" with "Current yield (at launch): 0%" for ETH (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.1.9.1.4.2.1), and "Max yield: 10%" with the same 0% launch rate for USDC and USDT (.9.2.4.2.1, .9.3.4.2.1). Each instance separately records a `Setter` address (.9.1.4.1.3, .9.2.4.1.3, .9.3.4.1.3).

Only the ceiling is a governance parameter. The live rate is operational, moved by the Setter within the authorised band, and the Artifact records where it started rather than where it must stay — the "(at launch)" qualifier says explicitly that this value is expected to be stale.

This is delegation with a bounded blast radius, the same pattern as the rate limits but applied to price rather than quantity. Governance decides the worst case it will tolerate; operations chooses inside it and can respond to market conditions in hours rather than through a proposal cycle. Setting a rate competitively is a continuous exercise that a deliberative process cannot perform well.

The honest cost is that the published number is not the real one. A reader learns the maximum Spark could be paying, not what it is paying, and the difference between 0% and 10% on a 2bn cap is the entire economics of the product. The Artifact is authoritative about the constraint and deliberately silent about the state — which is the right split for a governance document, provided readers do not mistake `Current yield (at launch)` for current yield.
description: Each product publishes a Max yield alongside a Current yield of 0% at launch, so the operative decision is the ceiling — the live rate is set inside it by whoever holds the Setter role.
